title: SNAP Participants Age 60+ Share, FY2024
question: USDA Food and Nutrition Service Characteristics of SNAP Households FY2024, SNAP QC sample, share of all SNAP participants who are age 60 or older, first print
resolutionSource: USDA Food and Nutrition Service Characteristics of SNAP Households: Fiscal Year 2024, Appendix Table A.29
resolutionRule: Resolve to 100 times Appendix Table A.29 elderly individuals age 60 or older divided by total participants in the first USDA FNS Characteristics of SNAP Households: Fiscal Year 2024 report, rounded to one decimal percentage point. Use the first public FY2024 report print posted on 2026-05-20; ignore later revised PDFs, addenda, or corrected tables unless USDA explicitly withdraws and replaces the first public report on the same posting date.

reasoning.text: Forecast for FY2024 SNAP Participant Share Age 60 Plus

Framing and exact resolver: the target is the USDA FNS annual SNAP Characteristics report, not the monthly SNAP participation tables. The variant is the FY2024 SNAP QC sample Appendix Table A.29, elderly individuals age 60 or older divided by total participants, first public report print.

reasoning.result: Fetched release page numbers: the FY2024 Characteristics page lists Final Report size 3.18 MB and page updated May 20, 2026; it describes FY2024 as the latest annual series report.

reasoning.call: Inspect USDA FNA data and research listing for release-date verification
reasoning.result: Fetched official listing numbers: Characteristics of SNAP Households: Fiscal Year 2024 is dated 05/20/2026; nearby SNAP program-data entries include February 2026 Keydata Report dated 05/14/2026 and March 2026 Keydata Report dated 06/18/2026.

reasoning.call: Inspect FY2024 report cover and executive summary
reasoning.result: Fetched report numbers: report number SNAP-24-CHAR, May 2026; FY2024 average monthly SNAP participation was 41.4 million people and 22.1 million households, with total federal cost $99.4 billion and average monthly household benefit $341.

reasoning.call: Inspect FY2024 Appendix Table A.29 for exact target numerator and denominator
reasoning.result: Fetched Appendix Table A.29 numbers: FY2024 total participants 40,344 thousand and elderly individuals age 60 or older 8,004 thousand; computed share is 8,004 / 40,344 * 100 = 19.8 percent.

reasoning.call: Inspect FY2018-FY2023 Appendix Table A.29 same-series history
reasoning.result: Fetched same-table history: FY2018 total 39,519 thousand and 60+ 5,579 thousand = 14.1 percent; FY2019 total 37,202 and 60+ 5,800 = 15.6 percent; FY2020 pre-pandemic total 36,363 and 60+ 5,887 = 16.2 percent; FY2022 total 39,246 and 60+ 7,181 = 18.3 percent; FY2023 total 40,065 and 60+ 7,807 = 19.5 percent.

reasoning.call: Inspect USDA report series page for publication reference class
reasoning.result: Fetched report-series publication numbers: FY2023 was published April 2025, FY2022 in June 2024, FY2020 in June 2022, FY2019 in March 2021, FY2018 in November 2019, and there was no FY2021 report because data were incomplete.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the same-series Appendix Table A.29 history had moved from 14.1 percent in FY2018 to 19.5 percent in FY2023, with no FY2021 report. The reference class is annual SNAP QC characteristics releases using the same age-60-or-older participant count over total participants, not administrative monthly caseload totals.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanism: the level entering FY2024 was high at 19.5 percent. Momentum was upward but should slow after the FY2022-FY2023 jump. One-off pandemic administrative waivers and emergency allotments had already unwound, and FY2024 ABAWD age-limit changes affected ages below 60 rather than directly moving the elderly numerator.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is FY2023 same-series share 7,807 / 40,065 * 100 = 19.486 percent. Historical sample for uncertainty uses successive same-series changes through the latest pre-FY2024 history: 2018-2019 +1.473, 2019-2020 +0.599, 2020-2022 +2.108, 2022-2023 +1.188 percentage points, so sigma = sqrt((1.473^2 + 0.599^2 + 2.108^2 + 1.188^2) / 4) = 1.448. The normal 80% half-width is roughly 1.28*sigma = 1.28*1.448 = 1.85 points. Because the first print is already public at run time, the point is pinned to the fetched first-print value 19.8; applying the pre-release-style 1.85-point half-width gives 19.8 - 1.85 = 18.0 and 19.8 + 1.85 = 21.6 after one-decimal rounding.

Counter-consideration: upside risk would be a much larger-than-expected fall in nonelderly SNAP participation or continued rapid aging of the caseload, which would land above the interval if the share exceeded 21.6 percent. Downside risk would be renewed nonelderly caseload growth or sampling/weighting changes lowering the older-adult composition, which would land below the interval if under 18.0 percent. An outside the interval outcome would more likely indicate a reporting-definition change or unusually large QC sample composition shift than ordinary trend continuation.
